articleTitle: Hybrid techniques in antenna measurements: the semi-compact range
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: Hybrid techniques developed over the past decade essentially combine the attributes of compact ranges and near-field to far-field transformation methods. These perform the integration along one of the two axes in real time with the use of a suitable line source probe and, thereafter, require the measurement of a single array of data along a single cut over the other axis. Data acquisition requirements are reduced with faster processing algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessment of a technique for measurement of antenna G/T using solar noise
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: A fundamental measure of the sensitivity of a microwave receiving system could be estimated directly and simply from a measurement of the ratio of the noise output of the system when the antenna is pointed at the sun, to that when the antenna is pointing at 'cold' sky. The purpose of the work described was to assess the achievable accuracy of the technique, and to identify the critical aspects of such a measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave holography applications in antenna development
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: Microwave holography is well established for the evaluation and optimisation of electrically large reflector antennas used for satellite ground stations. Increasing interest has been shown for using the method during development of other complex antenna configurations in order to improve the design, minimise design cycles and reduce the overall cost. Two application examples of the development of high performance antennas are presented: a corrugated slotted waveguide array antenna operating at 19.95 GHz, where the design has been optimised on the basis of results obtained from microwave holography, and a 3.4m diamond reflector for SATCOM applications operating at 14 GHz where surface profile distortions have been quantified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of the HP 85301A antenna measurement system to receiver pattern measurements
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: This paper provides a brief description of the standard HP 85301A system, and primarily addresses adaptation of the standard system for measurement of Phalanx missile receiver IF patterns. Measured IF pattern results obtained using the antenna test system are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-channel digital antenna pattern measurement for DF system calibration
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: The calibration of a broadband, dual-polarized direction finding system requires the measurement of an enormous quantity of accurate antenna pattern data, and the processing of that data into a digital format compatible with the system calibration algorithms. A high-speed multiplexing architecture has been implemented which permits interleaved measurements of 16 independent channels. The particular antenna system under consideration is a multi-element array consisting of four 2 to 18 GHz sinuous antennas. Phase and amplitude response must be measured for both vertical and horizontal polarizations on each output port at 201 frequencies. To fully characterize the antenna, azimuth patterns are measured at 9 different elevation angles. The data is collected in 1.0 degree increments over +or-90 degrees, and processed by a proprietary Antenna Measurement System and HP8530 Receiver operating in 'Turbo' mode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in wavefront quality assessment using superresolution techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: Anechoic chambers are designed for maximum plane wave purity within the quiet zone region in which the antenna measurement is performed. In practice the resulting wavefront is imperfect, containing phase and amplitude ripple and cross-polarisation components. This degrades the pattern measurement and limits the accuracy and usable frequency range of the chamber. If the properties of the wavefront may be accurately measured, the profile of the numerous illuminating sources (due to chamber wall reflections) could be determined by a Fourier transform and, by a de-convolution process, used to compensate measured patterns to reduce the effects of non-ideal chamber behaviour. The primary objective of this work is wavefront characteristic determination by MUSIC angular spectrum estimation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gain and pattern calibration of VHF antennas for an over-water propagation experiment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: Predicting the propagation loss of VHF and UHF signals as they travel over the ocean surface at near-grazing incidence is extremely difficult. The variability caused by wind and waves requires simplifying assumptions which call into question the validity of both analytical and numerical models. In order to provide solid experimental data, which can be used to validate proposed propagation models, a propagation test system is presented and its results are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of ARMS and LEGS for investigating novel antennas
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: Two antenna measurement systems allowing spherical far-field and planar near-field measurements were developed specifically to investigate small dielectric-loaded antennas because these measurement configurations allow the antenna under test to remain stationary with bore-sight vertical so that the dielectric lenses or pucks can be held in place by gravity. The paper describes the two systems and illustrates how they can be used to investigate novel dielectric antennas which are difficult to model theoretically.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of mutual coupling betwen phased array elements
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: Mutual coupling between a pair of identical array elements is calculated from the radiated far fields (Richmond, 1961) using the reaction theorem applied to a single element. Results for the far field reaction technique have been obtained for a Hertzian dipole and waveguide aperture model, tested on different reaction surfaces. Comparisons with more conventional calculations applicable to the chosen element clearly indicate increased accuracy. The method is hoped to provide a quick and easy estimation of the mutual coupling using the measured far field data of a single array element. This technique is intended to be used as a development tool for the design of phased array elements with low mutual coupling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Novel Antenna Measurement Techniques
abstract: The radiation patterns of a low (40 dB) sidelobe antenna have been measured on a variety of antenna test ranges including near field, far field and compact versions. Some of the early results are presented and the variations examined. The need for some form of range validation is shown. There is also some explanation of the fundamental effects of various ranges on results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
